**Ingredients**
- Frozen hash browns
- 4 strips bacon, chopped
- 1–2 jalapeños, sliced
- 1 tbsp avocado oil
- 1 cup freshly shredded Colby Jack (do NOT use pre-shredded)

**Method**
1. Air-fry hash browns and bacon until crisp.
2. In an oiled skillet over medium, lay down jalapeños. Top with a flat layer of Colby Jack.
3. Once the cheese starts to bubble and form a crust, plop the hash browns and bacon on top and press down.
4. Let the cheese fully crisp into a frico crust before flipping out, cheese-side up.

And yes, technically this is somewhere between a pâté and a rillette BUT “pâté your tinned fish” is much more fun. Thank you to my friends at @fishwife for sending over some product for me to cook with! 🌱Recipe below! 

#smokedfish #pate #cooking #homegrown #homemade 

BEFORE WE START.. You can customize this with whatever herbs & tinned fish you’ve got! Have fun :-)

Ingredients 
* 1 tin Fishwife smoked rainbow trout w/liquid included
* 1 stick room temp butter
* 1 garlic clove
* Juice of 1/2 of lemon
* A small handful of fresh herbs finely chopped
* Crostini & pickled red onion for serving

Preparation 
1. Cut the butter in half. Melt one half in a small pan and put the other half in a small bowl.
2. Chop your herbs and place them in the bottom of a ramekin or small mold. Pour the melted butter over the herbs and place in the freezer while you make the pâté.
3. Mix the room temperature butter with a fork.. Add the garlic and lemon juice, then pour in the **entire tin of smoked trout, liquid and all!!! Mix until well combined, leaving a little texture in the fish.
4. Spoon the trout mixture over the chilled herb butter and freeze for about 15 minutes until firm.
5. To unmold, take it straight from the freezer and let sit at room temp for a few minutes before using your hands to warm the outside of the glass or ramekin.. should flip out beautifully. If it doesn't’ just run a butter knife around the edge!

If you aren’t eating the whole thing at once, keep it frozen and cut off pieces as you go. Let each piece sit out for 10–15 minutes before serving.

reconstructed.body:
**Ingredients** (serves 1)
- 1 packet Daisho hot & spicy hot pot base (or any hot pot soup base)
- 1½ cups water
- Frozen thin-sliced beef (don't bother thawing)
- Napa cabbage, bok choy, sliced onion, tofu — whatever's hanging on in the fridge
- Cooked rice or noodles, for finishing

**Method**
1. In a pan or wok, combine water and the soup base. Bring to a boil.
2. Add the hardier veg (cabbage stems, onion) first. Simmer 2 min.
3. Add tofu and leafy greens.
4. Last, drop in the frozen beef slices and cook just until no longer pink, ~1 min.
5. Eat first bowl as soup; add rice or noodles to the leftover broth for round two.

reconstructed.title: One-Pot Cabbage Roll Soup
reconstructed.body:
**Ingredients** (serves 4–6)
- 1 lb ground beef or turkey
- 1 onion, diced; 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- ½ head green cabbage, chopped
- 6 cups chicken broth
- 2 tbsp white miso
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 block silken or soft tofu, cubed
- Cooked rice, optional

**Method**
1. Brown the ground meat in a pot. Add onion, garlic, ginger; cook until soft.
2. Add cabbage and broth. Simmer until cabbage is tender, ~15 min.
3. Stir in soy sauce. Whisk miso with a ladle of broth and stir back in (don't boil after).
4. Lay tofu on top, cover, and warm through 3 min.
5. Serve as-is or over rice.

1️⃣ Set a non-negotiable shut-down boundary at the end of the day.
👉 Pick a time. Close the laptop. Walk away. (And stop checking emails until the next work day!)

Think chukauni… but with juicy golden chicken, smoky mustard oil tadka, garlic-y curd, and those Nepali-style flavours that just hit different.
It’s rich, tangy, spicy, creamy — and honestly perfect with soft rotis or steaming hot rice.

Nepali Style Chicken Chukauni 
🥣 Serves: 3
🔥 Macros (per serving):
Calories: 374 kcal | Protein: 38 g | Carbs: 2.7 g | Fat: 22.3 g

Ingredients
For the Chicken
	•	400 g boneless chicken thigh (or breast), cut into small cubes
	•	2 tsp ginger-garlic paste
	•	½ tsp salt
	•	½ tsp pepper
	•	1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder
	•	½ tsp turmeric powder
	•	1 tsp lemon juice
	•	Light brush or spray of oil for frying
For the Mix
	•	1 small onion, thinly sliced
	•	1–2 green chilies, chopped
	•	3 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, chopped (divided)
For the Yogurt Base
	•	1 cup thick curd (I used Amul High-Protein Curd) or Greek yogurt 
	•	1 tsp garlic paste
	•	½ tsp salt
	•	½ tsp sugar
For the Tadka
	•	1.5 tbsp mustard oil
	•	½ tsp turmeric powder
	•	1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder
	•	1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed

Method
1️⃣ Mix chicken with ginger-garlic paste, salt, pepper, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, and lemon juice.
Rest 10–15 minutes.

2️⃣ Brush or spray a pan with very little oil.
Pan-fry chicken on medium-high until golden brown.
Transfer to a bowl.

3️⃣ Add sliced onion, chopped chilies, and half the coriander.
Mix well and set aside.

4️⃣ In another bowl, whisk thick curd with garlic paste, salt, and sugar until smooth and creamy.

5️⃣ Heat mustard oil until smoking hot.
Turn off the heat, add turmeric, Kashmiri chili powder, and crushed kasuri methi.

6️⃣ Pour the hot tadka into the curd and swirl gently to keep the streaks.

7️⃣ Pour the yogurt mixture over the chicken mixture. Mix gently. Finish with more chopped coriander leaves.
Enjoy with soft rotis or steaming hot rice.

*Jalapeños — I LOVE the jalapeños and the heat they bring in this recipe, so I use four. You can easily tone this down to one or two, or omit completely (but I wouldn’t recommend it). 

**Pickling spice — I’ve done this without pickling spice before by using 3T-worth of mustard seeds, peppercorns, allspice, star anise…things like this. I’ve even used mustard powder before, but it does make the brine a little murky. 

The ingredients on my current supply of pickling spice are: yellow and brown mustard seeds, allspice, cinnamon, bay leaves, dill seed, cloves, ginger, black peppercorns, star anise, coriander, juniper, mace, cardamom and crushed red pepper.

Ham + Cheese Hot Pockets
INGREDIENTS

Dough
-4 cups (500g) AP flour
-2 teaspoons (10g) kosherfine salt
-1 tablespoon (12g) sugar
-1 packet (7g) yeast (active dry or instant I don’t know the difference)
-1 1/4 cups (300g) warm water
-2 tablespoons (30g) olive oil or melted butter

Filling
-8 ounces deli ham
-8 ounces mild cheddar, shredded

Topping
-2 ounces salted butter, melted
-Flaky salt
-Poppy seeds, optional

Dough Instructions
1. Combine dry ingredients: flour, salt, sugar, and yeast.
2. Add warm water + oil. Mix until it becomes a rough dough.
3. Knead (8 minutes) or stand mix (5 minutes) until smooth.
4. Cover 1 to 1.5 hours until dough rises and doubles in size..
5. Divide into 12 balls. Rest 10 minutes before filling.

Filling + Bake
1. Flatten or roll each dough ball to about 4” across.
2. Add ham + cheddar. Close + pinch to seal; place seam-side down.
3. Cut tiny slits to vent. Brush w/ butter, salt ,and poppy seeds.
4. Bake at 425°F for 15-18 min until golden.
